newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. City Council bill would curb Burma dealings.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. City Council bill would curb Burma dealings.

text.p: The New York City Council, which sought to prod Swiss banks into accounting for how they treated Holocaust victims, on Tuesday said it would hold hearings on a proposal to curb the city's dealings with Burma.

The city council said it was considering the measure because of alleged human rights violations by Burma's State Law and Order Restoration Council, which seized power in 1988 after crushing a pro-democracy uprising.

Describing the measure as largely symbolic, Tom McMahon, the council's director of finance, last week said that the next step would be to restrict the city's pension investments. "But that's down the road," he said.
A spokesman for the city comptroller had no information immediately available on whether New York City had any Burma pension investments.
McMahon said he expected the city council would approve the measure against Burma shortly after the hearings.
If the bill were enacted, the city would be following similar moves by the U.S. government, which has suspended all economic and military aid to Burma, the city council said.
Massachusetts has also barred companies from doing business with the state if they did business in Burma.
